features.breakout: 144 sub-rate ports maximum (10/25/50GbE) or 128 at 40/100GbE using breakout cables
features.optics-qsfp-dd: 10GBASE-CR/SR/LR/ER, 25GBASE-CR/SR/LR/ER, 40GBASE-CR4/SR4/LR4/ER4, 100GBASE-CR4/SR4/LR4/ER4/DR1/PSM4/CWDM4, 400GBASE-CR4/SR4/FR4/DR4/LR8 (guide Port Descriptions); DAC up to 3 m (datasheet)
features.timing: IEEE 1588 1-step and 2-step, TC and BC, SyncE (timing option)

management.console: RJ45 RS-232, 115200 8N1, flow control XON/XOFF (labelled IOIOI)
management.usb: USB 2.0 host type A, data only (does not supply power)

performance.latency: less than 700 ns port to port (cut-through)

platform.bmc: BMC management option (DDR3, SPI flash dual boot, NC-SI shared port, IPMI 2.0)
platform.cpu: Intel Xeon D-1627 4-core or D-1649N 8-core on a COMe module (per SKU)

b2f.description: R4023-F9003-A0 - back-to-front airflow, 4-core Xeon D-1627, 1 x 16 GB DDR4, 64 GB SSD, two 1500 W AC supplies, seven fans. QSFP-DD power drops to 24 x 5 W + 8 x 12 W (ports 25-32). No held document shows whether the fans or supply latches change colour for this build, so the art is the f2b art (see the b2f-finish gap).

b2f-2x16g-128g.description: R4023-F9004-A0 - back-to-front, 4-core Xeon D-1627, 2 x 16 GB DDR4, 128 GB SSD, two 1500 W AC supplies, seven fans.

b2f-8c-256g.description: R4023-F9005-A0 - back-to-front, 8-core Xeon D-1649N, 2 x 16 GB DDR4, 256 GB SSD, two 1500 W AC supplies, seven fans.

f2b.description: R4023-F9102-A0 - front-to-back airflow, 4-core Xeon D-1627, 1 x 16 GB DDR4, 64 GB SSD, two 1500 W AC supplies and seven fans (guide What's in the Box, 'ASSY,TLA,DS4000,32X400GbE,4C D1627,1X16GB DDR4,64GB SSD,2X1500W AC PSU,7 FAN,F2B'). Drawn with the one-SFP+ front (M1 fitted, the M2 lanes routed as 10GBASE-KR - guide Figure 2), the build the DS4000 datasheet render shows; which front build each SKU ships with is not stated (see the front-build-sku gap).

f2b-2sfp.description: The two-SFP+ front (guide Figure 3, 'DS4000/DS4001 (2x SFP+)'): M1 over M2 at the right of the QSFP-DD block. An illustration of a build the guide draws; no SKU is tied to it.

f2b-2x16g-128g.description: R4023-F9103-A0 - front-to-back, 4-core Xeon D-1627, 2 x 16 GB DDR4, 128 GB SSD, two 1500 W AC supplies, seven fans. The control plane is the only difference from f2b, and nothing on the faces shows it.

f2b-8c-256g.description: R4023-F9104-A0 - front-to-back, 8-core Xeon D-1649N, 2 x 16 GB DDR4, 256 GB SSD, two 1500 W AC supplies, seven fans.

f2b-kr.description: The no-SFP+ front (guide Figure 1, 'DS4000/DS4001 (2x 10GKR)'): both SFP+ positions are blank panel and their lanes are routed internally as 10GBASE-KR. An illustration of a build the guide draws; no SKU is tied to it.

datasheet.title: Celestica DS4000 1U 32-port 400GbE Data Center Switch datasheet

description: Celestica DS4000 1U 32-port 400GbE data center switch - 32 QSFP-DD in two belly-to-belly rows of sixteen, up to two 10G SFP+ management ports (M1/M2) beside a vertical console RJ45 / USB-A / management RJ45 stack at the right of the front, and at the rear two 1500 W AC supplies (1+1) at either end of seven hot-swap fans (6+1). 12.8 Tbps, COMe Xeon D control plane. Sold front-to-back (R4023-F9102/F9103/F9104-A0) and back-to-front (R4023-F9003/F9004/F9005-A0). The DS4001 is a separate device with a different faceplate.

gaps.note: The guide draws three fronts (2x 10GKR, 1x SFP+ plus 1x 10GKR, 2x SFP+) and lists six chassis SKUs whose descriptions differ only in CPU, memory, SSD and airflow. Nothing held ties a front to a SKU. Re-read when the six SKUs became six orderable configurations: all six are drawn with the datasheet render's one-SFP+ front, which is the same unsourced choice made six times rather than a finding, and the other two fronts stay `example` configurations. If a SKU turns out to ship another front, its configuration takes `views: {front: ...}` and nothing else moves.
gaps.wanted: a Celestica ordering guide or SKU description naming the SFP+ build

gaps.note: The only rear render held is of a DS4001 (black fans, blue latches, orange PSU latches) and its airflow is not stated. The DS4100 rear, from the same vendor, is orange-faced, which may be an airflow colour code; no held DS4000/DS4001 document says so.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of each airflow build

gaps.note: The artwork prints STAT, FAN, PWR, ALM top to bottom; the guide's Front Panel Status LEDs table signs the same four SYS, ALM, PSU, FAN. The silkscreen follows the artwork and each lamp takes the table row for its function.
gaps.wanted: a front photograph of a DS4000

gaps.note: No held document names the FRU part numbers of the 1500 W supply or the fan module; the components are named for their form (celestica/psu-1500-ac, celestica/fan-40).
Neither the DS4000 datasheet nor the guide names the switching silicon. Distributor pages (Stordis) name Broadcom Tomahawk 3; that is not a Celestica document and is not carried as an attr.
gaps.wanted: a Celestica document naming the ASIC

attrs.redundancy-note: 6+1 - DS4000 datasheet, Power and Cooling: '6+1 redundant fans, front to back and back to front system cooling'; seven bays, and the SKU descriptions say '7 FAN'

mgmt.mixed: the management stack - RS-232 console RJ45, USB 2.0 host port and the CPU/BMC shared Ethernet management RJ45, on one silver plate

port-leds.description: four tri-colour lamps per QSFP-DD port (LED1-LED4, one per lane group in a 4-way breakout) and one per SFP+. Guide LED table: 8x10G amber (or white), 8x25G green (or white), 2x40G amber on LED1 and LED3, 4x40G amber, 4x50G green, 8x50G blue (or white), 2x100G green on LED1 and LED3, 4x100G blue, 2x200G blue on LED1 and LED3, 1x400G blue on LED1.

attrs.redundancy-note: 1+1 - What's in the Box describes every DS4000 chassis SKU with '2X1500W AC PSU', and the DS4000 datasheet says '1+1 redundant, hot swap PSUs'; two bays at the rear ends

sfp-plus-mgmt.description: the M1/M2 SFP+ position at the right of the QSFP-DD block - 10GbE per the guide's port table. Built as one SFP+ (M1, the datasheet render's build), two (Figure 3) or none, the lanes then routed internally as 10GBASE-KR (Figure 1); see the configurations.

status-leds.description: the four chassis lamps - STAT, FAN, PWR, ALM

name: ds4000

chassis.note: datasheet and guide specifications table agree - height 43.1 mm (1.73 in, 1 EIA unit), width 438.5 mm (17.3 in), depth 657.5 mm (25.8 in). 438.5 is the body; the front elevation's face measures the same 438.5 at the scale its own cage pitch implies, and the rack brackets (R3240-F0301-01, 'ASSY,FIXED BRACKET,L-BRACKET' in What's in the Box) are not drawn. No weight is stated in any held document.

colour.note: photo - the DS4000 datasheet render shows a BLACK face with white legends and silver cage shells; the guide's light grey is CAD shading. Chassis sheet metal is light grey in every render. So chassis.color is the sheet metal (#c4c8cc, which the top, bottom, sides and the rear frame between the modules wear - the rear webs are grey in the guide CAD and silver in the DS4001 rear render), and the black front bezel is a full-face decor rect under everything else on the front, since a view carries no colour of its own.

environment.note: The datasheet and the guide state different operating envelopes and both are carried: the datasheet 'Temperature: 0 C to 45 C @ 900m, Humidity: 5% to 90% non-condensing'; the guide's specifications table 'Operating Temperature (airflow front to back) 5 - 40 C', the same for back to front, 'Operating Relative Humidity 40 - 60 %', 'Storage Relative Humidity 5 - 95 %'. The operating-temp attr takes the datasheet's; the guide's narrower figures are in operating-temp-guide and operating-humidity-guide.

gate-1.note: The guide's front elevations are 1531-1532 x 156 px CAD exports (the same rasters are embedded in the PDF at 218 dpi, so the PDF holds no better image). The face spans x 2-1527 (1526 px) and y 2.5-154.5 (152 px): against 438.5 x 43.1 mm that is 3.4800 px/mm across and 3.527 down, 1.3 percent apart, the drawn height carrying the lid and base flange lines. The rear elevation (1686 x 172) gives 3.8404 and 3.898, 1.5 percent apart in the same direction. The figure is ORTHOGRAPHIC by the test that matters: the sixteen QSFP-DD column centres (cage outline edges found on dark-column runs at rows 40-68) fit a straight line at 0.36 px rms (0.10 mm) with a quadratic term worth 0.8 px across the whole row. So x is measured at 3.480 px/mm from the left face edge, and y is taken as a fraction of the drawn height scaled to 43.1 mm.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-09-26 for a DS4000/DS4001 end-of-life or end-of-sale announcement; none found. The Foleon product page, both datasheets and the documentation portal are live and the guide was revised in 2/2026.

mgmt.note: measured - a silver plate at x 406.9-423.8, y 6.73-38.63 holding, top to bottom, an RJ45 with its latch keyway UP (console: the 'IOIOI' legend beside it, and the guide's Connecting a Console page), a USB-A (USB 2.0 host, data only - Product Overview note), and an RJ45 with its keyway DOWN and two lamp windows in its lower corners (management; network symbol beside it). Jack openings 12.9 mm wide, matching std/rj45-ganged@2's 12.7 cell rather than the 15.8 mm single housing; the console is rotate 180 because the std part draws the keyway down. The USB is USB 2.0 (guide port table), so std/usb-a@1 is seated with its usb2 skin. To their right a vertical pull-out lug tag (celestica/lug-tag@1, turned on end) in a slot, x 430.5-433.5, y 16.1-39.3. THE LUG TAG IS SEATED WITH NO LABEL, on purpose. The DS4001 render prints its model on the tag and the ES1000 figure its; for the DS4000 the held images were read for it at 8x - the datasheet render (1005 x 477) shows a faint mark on the tag a few pixels high that does not resolve into characters, the Foleon ds4000-A-white render is untextured and prints nothing, and the guide CAD draws the tag blank. Writing 'DS4000' there would be a guess that looks like a reading. The 'Celestica' wordmark over the plate is not in the CAD; it is printed there on the DS4000 datasheet render and the DS4001 render, set here as plain text, not a logo.

model-split.note: THE GUIDE'S FRONT FIGURES ARE THIS DEVICE, NOT THE DS4001, although they are captioned 'DS4000/DS4001'. The guide covers both models and draws one front, with the SFP+ position at the RIGHT of the QSFP-DD block beside the status lamps. The DS4000 datasheet render and the Foleon ds4001.png render both show that layout; the DS4001 datasheet render and the Foleon ds4001_front render (pull tab printed 'DS4001') show an SFP+ pair at the LEFT end instead, a hexagon-vented face and 'HP' port legends. So the guide front is modelled here and the DS4001 is modelled from its own renders. The rear, the LED tables and the specifications table are the guide's shared ones and apply to both.

part-numbers.note: Six chassis SKUs, from the guide's What's in the Box Table 1 (PDF rev 1.4.0): R4023-F9102/F9103/ F9104-A0 front-to-back and R4023-F9003/F9004/F9005-A0 back-to-front, differing within an airflow only in CPU (4C D1627 or 8C D1649N), memory (1 or 2 x 16 GB) and SSD (64, 128 or 256 GB). Each is its own orderable configuration with its own part-numbers entry, because the DCIM exporter makes one device type per configuration SKU and a configuration listing three would export one. The control-plane figures live in the descriptions: a configuration carries no attrs of its own (see the config-scoped-device-attrs gap on cisco/asr-9001) and a part-numbers entry holds only part and power-cord. The datasheet's ordering lines name only F9102 and F9003.

port-leds.note: The guide's QSFP-DD Port LED Locations page: 'Each QSFP-DD port has four tri-color LEDs Blue/Green/Amber', with a close-up of port 31 labelling LED1 over LED2 at the cage's upper left and LED3 over LED4 at its upper right. Measured on the front elevation at 8x: round windows 2.0 mm across at x = column centre -8.0 and +8.0 mm, at y 4.54 and 7.26 above the top-row cage and y 35.16 and 37.85 below the bottom-row cage, the same four per port on all sixteen columns. Drawn as common/led-dot@1. WHICH window is LED1 for a BOTTOM-row port is not shown - the close-up is of an upper port - so the lower port's windows are numbered in the same reading order (left column top to bottom, then right), which is an inference. The LED table maps each colour to a breakout mode (8x10G through 1x400G); the colours are carried as states and the mode table is summarised in the port-leds group description.

port-power.note: guide, QSFP-DD Port Power Outputs - front-to-back builds 28 x 15 W + 4 x 20 W (ports 1, 2, 31, 32 at 20 W); back-to-front builds 24 x 5 W + 8 x 12 W (ports 25-32 at 12 W). The DS4000 datasheet says 'Up to 12W in Back to Front airflow' and 'Up to 20W in Front to Back airflow', which agrees.

power.note: datasheet - '1100W peak consumption with 12W QSFP-DD, 1+1 redundant, hot swap PSUs'; '100-240VAC auto-ranging, 47-63Hz or 180-300VDC auto input'. The 1100 W is the vendor's figure with its own scope ('with 12W QSFP-DD', i.e. optics fitted) and is carried as power-max-w with envelope fully-configured; it is not reconciled against the supplies. PSU rating 1500 W each (What's in the Box).

qsfp-layout.note: measured - Figure 2 (and identically Figures 1 and 3): sixteen cage columns, outline centres at 24.33 + 22.894k mm (k = 0..15), outline width 19.95 mm; top-row cage outline y 9.33-19.39, bottom-row 22.84-33.14, i.e. 10.06 and 10.3 mm tall and 13.6 mm apart centre to centre. std/qsfp-dd@1 (19.0 x 10.0 registry opening) is centred in each outline and the outline itself is drawn as a silver cage-shell decor rect 20.0 x 10.3, because the std part draws only the opening. Numbering from the legends printed between the rows ('1 up 2 down' at column 1 through '31 up 32 down' at column 16): odd ports on the top row, even on the bottom, left to right. Rows follow the library stack rule, upper rotate 0 and lower 180; the CAD draws the upper cage's latch window at its top and the lower cage's at its bottom, which is the belly-to-belly pattern and so needs no exception.

rear.note: measured - Figure 4 at 3.8404 px/mm across, 3.898 down. Left to right: a chassis strip x 0-10.9 carrying an earth symbol at y 16.4 and two pan-head screws with copper washers at y 24.2 and 33.35 (the Grounding page: 'Attach grounding bracket to designated location on the chassis using the provided hardware', and its figure shows exactly these two screws taking the bracket); PSU2 at x 10.95-66.15; a web printed 'PWR2' with a triangle pointing at it; seven fans on 43.96 mm from x 70.21, each followed by a web printed 'FANk' with a triangle pointing LEFT at the fan it names, so FAN7 is leftmost and FAN1 beside PSU1; PSU1 at x 377.3-432.5, and 'PWR1' in the 6 mm strip after it. Both supplies face the same way (not mirrored). The module geometry is on celestica/psu-1500-ac@1 and celestica/fan-40@1. An independent reading of the same guide's rear callout by the DS4100 modeller put the PSUs at 10.5-66.4 and 377.2-432.9 and the fans at 70.5 + 44.02k, within 0.4 mm.

sfp-and-status.note: measured - Figure 3 draws two SFP+ cages stacked at x 380.7-396.3 (15.55 wide), y 9.04-19.85 and 22.68-33.14, one green lamp above the top cage and one below the bottom cage at x 385.4, and the legend 'M1 up-down M2' between them; Figure 2 draws the top cage only with 'M1 up'; Figure 1 draws neither. common/sfp-plus-cage@2 (16 x 10) is centred on 388.5. The four status lamps are 3.6 mm windows at x 401.9 on a 5.0 mm pitch from y 11.9 (measured 11.88, 16.84, 21.80, 26.93, set on one pitch), their legends set diagonally at about 60 degrees to their left. The legends read STAT, FAN, PWR, ALM at 14x zoom - the artwork's words; the guide's Table 1 signs them SYS, ALM, PSU, FAN in a different order. The lamps carry Table 1's meanings matched by function and the silkscreen carries the artwork's words.

sources.note: DS4000 datasheet (cls_datasheet_DS4000.pdf, 2 pp) for dimensions, interfaces, power, cooling, environment, approvals and ordering lines; the DS4000/DS4001 Installation Guide, both as the docs-portal HTML pages staged in the intake and as the 49-page PDF revision 1.4.0 (2/2026) at www.celestica.com/DS4000-installation-guide-v1, for the specifications table, the three front elevations (Product Overview Figures 1-3), the rear elevation (Figure 4), the LED tables, the QSFP-DD LED-location figure and table, the QSFP-DD power-class table, the What's in the Box SKU tables and the grounding pages; and three vendor product renders for colour and for telling the two models apart - the DS4000 datasheet's own three-quarter render (embedded 1005 x 477 px), and the Foleon product page's ds4001.png (a DS4000-layout render despite its name, untextured) and ds4001-side-by-side (the rear). No photograph of a real unit is held, and no square-on vendor photo of either face exists on the Foleon page.

vents.note: The CAD face is perforated almost everywhere there is no port. Drawn cell by cell as dark rects in the CAD's own shape: three 3.0 mm square cells between each column's lamp pairs, above the top row (y 3.9-6.9) and below the bottom row (y 35.3-38.3), at column centre -5.5, -1.55 and +2.4 mm (measured on column 1 at 8x and repeated on the pitch); a three-column grid of cells at the left end (x 1.0-12.3, nine rows on 4.0 mm) and one column at the right end (x 434.6-437.2). The cell grid at the ends is regularised - the CAD's cells there vary in width - and the rows of small cells along the lid and base edges and around the SFP and lamp area are not drawn. The small coloured vertical pips the CAD draws between cage columns are left out: no held document says what they are.

views.note: TOP: y = 0 is the REAR (house convention). The guide's isometric (Product Overview, first figure) and all three renders show two perforated fields on the lid - one against the left edge a little forward of mid-depth, one against the right edge a little behind it - rows of perforation along both side edges of the front third, and a recessed lid-release plate in the rear third on the centreline. Their positions are FRACTIONS off a perspective isometric and are estimated; the triangular fields are drawn as rectangles. BOTTOM carries the library's compliance-sticker placeholder, position estimated. LEFT (x = 0 is the rear) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the front) carry four rail fasteners each at estimated positions - the isometric shows a row of fasteners along the side, and the Chassis Installation page secures the outer rail bracket with M4 screws, but no figure dimensions them.
